nodes.label: AMLTRIX concept
nodes.comment:
Abstract parent of every catalogue entry (tactic, technique, ...). Label = skos:prefLabel, ID = skos:notation, text = skos:definition.

Data properties: STIX identifier, short description

nodes.label: Tactic
nodes.comment: A stage of the laundering process (e.g. Layering). A technique may serve several tactics.

nodes.label: Technique
nodes.comment: A method of laundering. Plays the role of a typology.

nodes.label: Sub-technique
nodes.comment: A refinement of exactly one parent technique, linked with skos:broader.

nodes.label: Indicator
nodes.comment: An observable red flag, owned by one technique.

nodes.label: Mitigation
Actor
nodes.comment: A persona or institution type that takes part in laundering (e.g. Cardholder, Insurance Company).

nodes.label: Value instrument
nodes.comment: A vehicle that stores or moves value (e.g. Casino Chips).

nodes.label: Product or service
Data source
nodes.comment: Where evidence of a technique can be observed.

nodes.label: Risk type
Transaction
nodes.comment:
One payment from one account to another. The data is synthetic.

Data properties: amount (logarithm), is cross-currency, is same bank, is self-transfer, payment format, timestamp

nodes.label: Account
nodes.comment:
An account that sends or receives payments. Only its identifier is known: there is no table of accounts, customers or companies.

Data properties: account id

nodes.label: Alert
nodes.comment:
One detection system flagged one payment. The same payment can have one alert from each system.

Data properties: ML score, source system

nodes.label: Flag
nodes.comment: A reason a detection system gives for an alert: one of the six rules, or the round trip found by the transaction graph.

nodes.label: Structuring
nodes.comment: Same account makes 2 or more same-day transactions in the $8,500-$10,000 range.

nodes.comment: An inflow of at least $3,000 followed within 3 days by an outflow of at least 85% of it from the same account (rapid pass-through).

    skos:definition "Funnel accounts involve depositing illicit proceeds in one location—often below reporting thresholds—and rapidly transferring or withdrawing them elsewhere, thereby obfuscating the origin of funds and frustrating investigators’ attempts to track a cohesive trail. Criminals commonly deposit structured amounts of cash into an individual or business account in one region, then withdraw or transfer the funds from a different location shortly thereafter. This tactic is also exploited to facilitate trade-based money laundering: multiple funnel accounts may consolidate into a single account that issues payments for the purchase of goods, creating a façade of legitimate transactions. Additionally, funnel accounts have been observed in human trafficking networks, where perpetrators maintain or coerce control over accounts in different locales, directing victims or third parties to deposit illicit proceeds into these accounts before swiftly removing the funds.     skos:definition "Informal Value Transfer Systems (IVTS) are networks used to transfer money or value outside formal banking channels, relying on personal trust or offset arrangements rather than regulated processes. Common examples include hawala or Chinese underground banks, where operators settle accounts via reciprocal transactions, off-the-books ledgers, or trade-based offsets in place of standard wire transfers. This setup allows criminals to bypass conventional AML/KYC controls, moving significant amounts of illicit proceeds discreetly across borders. In some jurisdictions, these parallel settlement schemes function as a separate, shadow-like infrastructure that evades regulated financial channels. Because documentation is minimal and operations can span multiple regions, IVTS transactions are difficult to trace, making these systems highly susceptible to money-laundering abuse. Many IVTS operators serve diaspora communities or regions with limited official banking services, blending legitimate remittances with illicit funds. Heavy reliance on personal trust underpins these arrangements, reducing overhead but obscuring the origin and destination of the proceeds. Violations of this trust can lead to reputational or communal repercussions for operators and participants, which in turn helps enforce compliance within these networks despite the absence of formal contracts. Some professionals engaging in IVTS also employ specialized software to move funds through multiple offset accounts, further complicating investigations. With lax or varied regulation across jurisdictions, IVTS continue to provide a hidden corridor for cross-border value transfers and remain a favored laundering channel for criminals seeking to structure, layer, or disguise proceeds from numerous predicate offenses."@en ;
    skos:inScheme <https://example.org/amltrix/scheme/amltrix-ml> ;
    skos:notation "T0013" ;
    skos:prefLabel "Informal Value Transfer Systems"@en ;

nodes.label: Alert
nodes.comment:
A flag raised by monitoring (a rule, a model or a graph analysis) on some activity.

Data properties: alert id, fact, raised at, trigger reason

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.comment: A piece of material gathered for an alert or case. Its kind is given by inv:recordType, an AMLTRIX data source type.

nodes.label: Checklist item
nodes.comment:
One suggested line of enquiry for an alert: an AMLTRIX indicator to look into, why it matters for this alert, how urgent it is, and which kind of records would show it. Advice only: no data is queried.

Data properties: priority, reason

nodes.label: Case
nodes.comment:
An investigation opened on one or more alerts.

Data properties: case id, opened at

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.comment:
An investigator's assessment of one AMLTRIX indicator within a case.

Data properties: observation, status

nodes.label: Report draft
nodes.comment:
A draft narrative for a case. It always requires investigator review.

Data properties: review status

nodes.label: Paragraph
nodes.comment:
One paragraph of a report draft, tied to the findings it rests on.

Data properties: text

nodes.label: Transaction
nodes.comment: An R2RML mapping. SQL: SELECT tx_id, ts, from_account, to_account, amount_log, is_cross_currency, is_self_transfer, is_same_bank, CASE WHEN fmt_wire = 1 THEN 'wire' WHEN fmt_ach = 1 THEN 'ach' WHEN fmt_cheque = 1 THEN 'cheque' WHEN fmt_cash = 1 THEN 'cash' WHEN fmt_credit_card = 1 THEN 'credit card' WHEN fmt_bitcoin = 1 THEN 'bitcoin' WHEN fmt_reinvestment = 1 THEN 'reinvestment' END AS payment_format FROM txs
nodes.ttl:
map:TransactionMap a rr:TriplesMap ;
    rr:logicalTable [ rr:sqlQuery """
        SELECT tx_id, ts, from_account, to_account, amount_log,
               is_cross_currency, is_self_transfer, is_same_bank,
               CASE WHEN fmt_wire = 1 THEN 'wire' WHEN fmt_ach = 1 THEN 'ach' WHEN fmt_cheque = 1 THEN 'cheque'
                    WHEN fmt_cash = 1 THEN 'cash' WHEN fmt_credit_card = 1 THEN 'credit card'
                    WHEN fmt_bitcoin = 1 THEN 'bitcoin' WHEN fmt_reinvestment = 1 THEN 'reinvestment' END AS payment_format
        FROM txs""" ] ;
    rr:subjectMap [ rr:template "https://example.org/transaction/{tx_id}" ; rr:class fcd:Transaction ] ;
    rr:predicateObjectMap
        [ rr:predicate fcd:timestamp ;       rr:objectMap [ rr:column "ts" ; rr:datatype xsd:dateTime ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:fromAccount ;     rr:objectMap [ rr:template "https://example.org/account/{from_account}" ; rr:termType rr:IRI ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:toAccount ;       rr:objectMap [ rr:template "https://example.org/account/{to_account}" ; rr:termType rr:IRI ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:amountLog ;       rr:objectMap [ rr:column "amount_log" ; rr:datatype xsd:double ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:isCrossCurrency ; rr:objectMap [ rr:column "is_cross_currency" ; rr:datatype xsd:boolean ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:isSelfTransfer ;  rr:objectMap [ rr:column "is_self_transfer" ; rr:datatype xsd:boolean ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:isSameBank ;      rr:objectMap [ rr:column "is_same_bank" ; rr:datatype xsd:boolean ] ] ,
        [ rr:predicate fcd:paymentFormat ;   rr:objectMap [ rr:column "payment_format" ] ] .

nodes.label: IND02195

nodes.label: IND02197

nodes.ttl: amx:IND02197 align:needsTerm amd:Shipment , amd:Invoice .

nodes.label: IND02198
nodes.comment: Frequent establishment and dissolution of trading entities, alongside repeated changes to account or ownership details, all lacking transparent operational explanations.
